name: Log4Shell - Apache Log4j JNDI remote code execution
description: Log4j 2 evaluates JNDI lookups in logged strings, letting attackers load remote code. Still scanned and exploited years later, with new obfuscation variants.
mitigation: Upgrade Log4j to 2.17.1 or later
If upgrade is impossible, remove the JndiLookup class from the log4j-core jar
Block outbound LDAP/RMI from servers
Inventory all Java apps and bundled jars

name: Baron Samedit - sudo heap overflow to root
description: Heap-based buffer overflow in sudo (before 1.9.5p2) lets any local user gain root.
mitigation: Upgrade sudo to 1.9.5p2 or later
Verify with: sudo --version

name: PwnKit - polkit pkexec local privilege escalation
description: pkexec mishandles empty argument lists, giving local users root on most Linux distributions.
mitigation: Update the polkit package
Temporary workaround: chmod 0755 /usr/bin/pkexec

name: Dirty Pipe - Linux kernel arbitrary file overwrite
description: Flaw in pipe buffer handling (kernel 5.8+) lets unprivileged users overwrite read-only files and escalate to root. Fixed in 5.16.11, 5.15.25, 5.10.102.
mitigation: Update to a patched kernel and reboot
Verify with: uname -r

name: Dirty COW - Linux copy-on-write race condition
description: Race in the kernel memory subsystem allowed local privilege escalation; exploited in the wild.
mitigation: Apply the kernel patch for your distribution and reboot

name: regreSSHion - OpenSSH sshd signal handler race
description: Race condition in OpenSSH server 8.5p1-9.7p1 can allow unauthenticated remote code execution as root on glibc systems. Fixed in 9.8p1.
mitigation: Upgrade OpenSSH to 9.8p1 or your distro's patched build
Workaround: set LoginGraceTime 0 in sshd_config (risk: connection exhaustion)
Restrict SSH access with firewall rules

name: XZ Utils supply-chain backdoor
description: Malicious code in xz/liblzma 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 tarballs could compromise sshd on affected systemd-based distributions.
mitigation: Downgrade or update to a clean xz release (5.4.x or distro-fixed build)
Check version: xz --version

name: Heartbleed - OpenSSL memory disclosure
description: Missing bounds check in the TLS heartbeat extension leaked server memory including private keys.
mitigation: Upgrade OpenSSL to a fixed version
Regenerate private keys and certificates
Rotate user passwords and session secrets

name: EternalBlue - SMBv1 remote code execution
description: SMBv1 flaw exploited by WannaCry and NotPetya; unpatched or legacy systems remain targets.
mitigation: Install Microsoft update MS17-010
Disable SMBv1: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false
Block TCP 445 at the perimeter

name: PrintNightmare - Windows Print Spooler RCE
description: Print Spooler allows remote code execution and privilege escalation via driver installation.
mitigation: Install the July 2021 or later cumulative update
Disable Print Spooler on servers that do not print
Restrict Point and Print policies

name: Follina - Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool RCE
description: Office documents can invoke msdt.exe through a URL protocol to run code without macros.
mitigation: Install the June 2022 or later security update
Workaround: delete the ms-msdt registry protocol handler

name: Zerologon - Netlogon privilege escalation
description: Cryptographic flaw in Netlogon lets an attacker take over a domain controller.
mitigation: Install August 2020 update and the February 2021 enforcement update
Monitor Netlogon event IDs 5827-5831

name: Windows TCP/IP IPv6 remote code execution
description: Specially crafted IPv6 packets can trigger zero-click RCE on Windows 10, 11 and Server.
mitigation: Install the August 2024 security update
If IPv6 is unneeded, disable it on the interface

name: Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attacks
description: Attackers load legitimately signed but vulnerable kernel drivers to disable EDR and gain kernel access; new drivers are abused continuously.
mitigation: Enable HVCI / memory integrity
Enable the Microsoft vulnerable driver blocklist
Use WDAC/App Control to allow only needed drivers

name: Infostealer malware harvesting browser credentials and tokens
description: Commodity stealers delivered by malvertising and cracked software steal saved passwords, cookies and session tokens.
mitigation: Use a password manager instead of browser storage
Enable MFA with phishing-resistant keys
Keep Defender and SmartScreen enabled
Revoke sessions after any suspected infection

name: FORCEDENTRY - zero-click iMessage CoreGraphics exploit
description: Malicious PDF-in-GIF processed by CoreGraphics gave zero-click code execution; used by mercenary spyware. Fixed in iOS 14.8 and macOS 11.6.
mitigation: Update iOS/macOS to the latest version
Enable Lockdown Mode for high-risk users

name: BLASTPASS - ImageIO buffer overflow zero-click chain
description: Malicious image attachments exploited ImageIO (with CVE-2023-41061 in Wallet). Fixed in iOS 16.6.1 and macOS 13.5.2.
mitigation: Update to iOS 16.6.1+ / macOS 13.5.2+ or later
Enable Lockdown Mode if targeted

name: Mercenary spyware zero-click chains on iPhone
description: Commercial spyware vendors keep shipping new zero-click exploit chains against messaging and image-parsing components.
mitigation: Install iOS updates immediately
Enable Lockdown Mode
Reboot regularly
Report suspected compromise to Apple/Access Now

name: macOS infostealers (e.g. Atomic Stealer) via fake installers and paste-and-run lures
description: Malware distributed through cracked apps, malvertising and fake 'fix' instructions that make users paste Terminal commands.
mitigation: Install only from the App Store or notarized developers
Never paste Terminal commands from websites
Keep Gatekeeper and XProtect enabled
Use a password manager

name: Stagefright - Android media library remote code execution
description: Integer overflow in libstagefright allowed code execution via crafted MMS media; fixed in 2015 security patches.
mitigation: Install Android security patch level 2015-08-01 or newer
Replace devices that no longer receive updates

name: Android banking trojans abusing Accessibility services
description: Sideloaded apps request Accessibility permission to read screens, intercept OTPs and perform overlay fraud.
mitigation: Install apps only from Google Play
Never grant Accessibility to unknown apps
Keep Play Protect enabled
Review special app access in Settings

name: Pre-installed malware on low-cost Android devices
description: Some cheap Android devices ship with backdoored firmware that turns them into proxy or fraud botnet nodes.
mitigation: Buy certified devices from reputable vendors
Check Play Protect certification status
Factory-reset and replace suspicious devices

name: Harvest-now-decrypt-later: quantum threat to RSA and ECC
description: Adversaries store encrypted traffic today to decrypt it once quantum computers can break RSA/ECC key exchange.
mitigation: Inventory where RSA/ECC is used
Plan migration to NIST post-quantum standards (ML-KEM, ML-DSA)
Enable hybrid post-quantum TLS where supported

name: AI-generated phishing and voice-cloning social engineering
description: LLM-written lures and cloned voices make phishing and vishing far more convincing and scalable.
mitigation: Use phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2 passkeys)
Verify payment or credential requests out-of-band
Run updated awareness training

name: Package registry supply-chain attacks (typosquatting, malicious updates)
description: Malicious packages on npm, PyPI and similar registries steal secrets or add backdoors at install time.
mitigation: Pin and hash-lock dependencies
Use an internal proxy/allow-list
Run SCA and review new dependencies
Disable install scripts where possible

name: eBPF-based rootkits on Linux
description: Attackers are expected to abuse eBPF for stealthy persistence, hiding processes and network traffic from user-space tools.
mitigation: Restrict unprivileged eBPF: kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1
Monitor bpf() syscall use
Use kernel lockdown and signed modules
